Solution 2 matches the result I recall; I did not re-derive the general formula.

- **Solution 3:** its formula $\lceil (n-1)/3\rceil$ is the depth of $S/I(C_n)$ for the edge ideal, not the symbolic power of the cover ideal. It fails at $n=4$. There $J(C_4)=(x_1x_3,x_2x_4)$ is a complete intersection, so $J^{(t)}=J^t$ and $S/J^t$ is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 2, giving depth 2. The formula gives $\lceil 3/3\rceil = 1$.
- **Solution 1:** $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ passes the checks at $n=3$ and $n=4$, but it rests on an unverified ordered-matching claim for even $n$. It predicts depth 3 for $n=6$, which disagrees with $\lceil n/3\rceil = 2$. I could not settle the $n=6$ case by direct computation, so this rejection rests on my recollection of the published result.
- **Solution 2:** $\lceil n/3\rceil$ gives 1 at $n=3$ and 2 at $n=4$, matching the direct checks. It also matches what I recall as the published result of Hoa–Kimura–Terai–Trung (and Nguyen–Trung) for $t\ge 2$. Its justification is shaky, since it was adjusted to fit the $n=4$ check after the first guess failed.

CHOICE: 2
